IRREVERENTS — Creative North Star

Status: Living vision baseline \| 22 November 2026

Authority: User-originated decisions from the design conversation. This document distinguishes settled intent from examples and unresolved details.

# One-sentence promise

A colorful, secret-packed, interconnected 2D action-adventure where a shared party of gloriously irreverent adventurers can discover powers, solve problems creatively, sneak through impossible places, provoke the world into spectacular resistance, and turn emergent feats into legends.

# The emotional contract

The game should continually invite: “What if I tried THAT?” Discoveries reward curiosity. Stealth rewards finesse. Combat rewards force and collision. Pursuit rewards desperate improvisation. The world rewards disruption with genuine reactions. A memorable failure can feel better than a routine success.

# Creative contrasts

- Whimsical, inviting, legible world versus outrageously forceful, risky player actions.

- A society obsessed with destiny and stories versus heroes indifferent to assigned grand narratives.

- Masterful zero-alarm infiltrations versus spectacular failed stealth turning into glorious battles or escapes.

- Relatively powerful player characters versus escalating numbers, variety, and intensity of opposition.

- A serious apocalyptic main quest versus hundreds of more interesting doors, artifacts, vehicles, creatures, and opportunities.

- Short-term, fleeting experiences versus a Hall of Legends that physically preserves them as history.

# Reference DNA, not literal cloning

Kirby & the Amazing Mirror: interconnected, revisitable side-scrolling spaces; copy-like enemy powers; secrets; colorful GBA-era visual grammar.

LEGO Star Wars / LEGO Batman: broad character functional types, individually distinctive moves, party switching, revisits enabled by newly unlocked character types, approachable fights, goofy reactive hubs.

Marvel: Ultimate Alliance: discover characters, permanently expand roster, assemble a limited expedition team.

Grand Theft Auto: unsolicited vehicle hijacks, mischievous violence, civilian/guard reactions, escalating attention, possibility of retreating to cool off.

Need for Speed: Most Wanted / Blacklist: thrilling escalating pursuit; escapes feel most vivid when success appears unlikely; collisions and police blockades are enormous spectacle.

Super Smash Bros., Street Fighter, Kirby suplex: spectacular contact, hit-stop, knockback, slam and launch satisfaction.

The Matrix Reloaded (Neo vs many Agent Smiths): a powerful hero confronting enormous swarms, defeating many while gradually being overwhelmed.

Skyrim, Zelda chickens, LEGO cantina fights: provoke everyday NPCs; discover surprising consequences.

# The player’s available verbs

Explore, revisit, climb, fly, shrink, sneak, hide, investigate, converse, steal, pickpocket, acquire powers, swap characters, attack, grab, suplex, throw, launch, break, ignite, commandeer, drive, escape, interfere, rescue, destroy, discover, memorialize. Not all verbs are guaranteed for all characters or all contexts.

# Non-negotiable experience principles

1. The overworld is real playable space, not a decorative level-select screen. Secret rooms and unlockable regions exist inside and between destination worlds.

2. Progress is nonlinear; a hard boss should seldom be the one mandatory gate to everything else.

3. Players are generally much stronger than ordinary enemies; variety, physicality and extreme escalation create combat enjoyment.

4. Stealth is a systemic approach, not a handful of scripted stealth missions.

5. Creative ability application matters more than merely matching a character icon to a door.

6. Players may provoke NPCs, start fights and attract expanding resistance, then hide, escape or keep fighting.

7. Alarm activation is not a “reload now” failure: it opens a new and often equally excellent action experience.

8. Cooperative online play works through one shared expedition party.

9. Epic stealth, last stands and escapes can be commemorated when players were participants.

10. The world takes its story and morality seriously; the playable heroes largely do not.

11. The world, including its royal court and Hall of Legends, remains playable and reactive.

12. Do not hard-code away emergent solo solutions to puzzles anticipated for simultaneous cooperation.

# Art direction baseline

Current preferred direction is strongly evocative of Kirby & the Amazing Mirror’s visual design: bright, whimsical, legible side-view environments and tiny expressive sprites, lively pixel-art detail, strong silhouettes, dense secrets and clear traversal. Initial “2D world with 3D-ish art” intent was revised toward a much closer Amazing Mirror visual reference; exact production technology and pixel density remain undecided. Current exploration art is concept material, not production-ready approved sprites.

# Confirmed versus undecided

Confirmed: title Irreverents; name is player-facing only, not a name the cast uses for itself in-world; nonlinear secret-rich platform-adventure; temporary acquired abilities/weapons; discoverable permanent roster with LEGO-like types; limited shared expedition party; online co-op; stealth; dynamic mayhem and pursuit; highly satisfying impact; Hall of Legends; irreverent anti-story protagonists; royal audience running gag.

Not fixed: final story ending, cast names, exact party size, co-op player maximum, roster count, power inventory rules, physics implementation, destructibility budgets, AI architecture, rating/violence presentation, release platforms, camera specifics, business scope, monetization, and engine.

# How to use this library

Read the Decision Register before treating an example as a requirement. The gameplay docs describe intended observable behavior rather than an engine blueprint. Scenarios are references for prototyping and playtesting. The original conversation contains many “imagine” examples; if not explicitly accepted, they are illustrative, not locked content.

D&D INSPIRATION — CHAOTIC NEUTRAL + RULE OF COOL (OWNER DIRECTION, 22 NOV 2026)

Irreverents is intentionally an HOMAGE TO CHAOTIC NEUTRAL AND THE RULE OF COOL in tabletop RPG play. The heroes are not defined by serving good, evil, law, justice, rebellion or prophetic significance. Their immediate compass is “What would be most EPIC?” or “Wouldn't it be awesome if…?” This can produce perfect stealth, inventive rescue, audacious heists, epic grappling, reckless challenges, gleeful accidents, vehicular chaos or monumental last stands. Chaotic Neutral must not be flattened to random cruelty, murderhobo behavior or compulsory disruption. They can choose the conventional heroic action if they genuinely find it cool.

RULE OF COOL is a game-design philosophy: reward imaginative, physically understandable player experiments by supporting compelling outcomes. Do not automatically grant success or ignore all world rules; a spectacular failure can be legendary. The game should honor the player's surprising intention and permit systemic consequences rather than require only one “correct” scripted solution.

The social contrast: much of the world is profoundly NARRATIVELY LAWFUL, including proud heroes and proud villains who adore their assigned good/evil role. The player party is the outlier. “Lawful” is a useful interpretive D&D analogy, not a decided literal in-world D&D alignment score.

OWNER-CORRECTED LEVEL TONE — GAMEPLAY FIRST, LITTLE DIALOGUE (22 NOV 2026)

Irreverents should feel like a Kirby or LEGO Star Wars-style 2D action-adventure: superb movement, readable enemies, secrets, powers, co-op puzzles, stealth, explosive fights and interesting geography. NOT every room or level should exist to restate the Hero's Journey joke or deliver lore. Character archetypes and joyful script obsession are the SETTING'S BACKGROUND; the player learns them mainly through behavior, expressions, poses, canned short barks and escalating reactions. Spoken/text dialogue should be sparse as in the named game inspirations. Silence and uncomplicated playful platform levels are desirable. Only rare well-placed major scenes, such as the intentionally endless opening king's speech, should indulge in substantial narrative presentation. Avoid forcing a thematic gimmick, special NPC speech or lore justification into each stage. Any playful title in level brainstorms is optional and not content canon.
